comparison: Perfect agreement on working memory impairment claims (C5, C37-C54). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with strong endorsement. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple behavioral assays and control experiments; peer reviewers describe findings as 'striking,' 'convincing,' and note 'exceptional' strength of evidence.

Strong agreement on longer-term memory findings (C55-C62). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes specificity strengthens working memory findings; peer reviewers accept these negative results without challenge and explicitly acknowledge the contrast between working memory and longer-term memory effects. Peer result also includes C6 (postsynaptic compartmentalization context).

Strong agreement on compartment-specific effects (C63-C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes postsynaptic targeting verification and remote fear memory impairment; peer reviewers explicitly affirm compartmentalized role and accept selective impairment without challenge. OpenEval includes C6 while peer review does not, but both address postsynaptic specificity.

Agreement on ultrastructural findings (C78-C86). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes statistical support for vesicle size and distance changes but flags speculative interpretations in C82, C84, C86; peer reviewers accept findings as 'verification of presynaptic efficacy' without raising concerns. OpenEval includes C9-C10 which are not in peer result.

Partial agreement on proteomic data (C7-C8, C87-C101). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats about mechanistic speculation; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN with significant reservations about lack of functional validation and follow-up on BioID/phosphoproteomic hits. Both acknowledge the data quality but question mechanistic conclusions.

Partial agreement on integrative model (C102-C105). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes interpretations extend beyond direct evidence; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, supporting behavioral compartmentalization but questioning mechanistic details and noting the scheme is 'necessarily vague.' Both identify gap between data and mechanistic conclusions.

Perfect agreement on W56 methodology validity (C34-C36). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites prior literature establishing effectiveness; peer reviewers explicitly accept the approach and state they are 'convinced that the presynaptic Rac1 function was successfully tweaked.'

Agreement on background literature (C1-C4, C11-C32). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these establish context but are not novel findings; peer reviewers do not challenge established facts and implicitly accept background by acknowledging prior literature. Peer result also includes synaptotagmin background claims (C106-C111) not in OpenEval R9.

Both address synaptotagmin phosphorylation (C106-C111). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting functional significance remains speculative and requires validation; peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but group these with broader background claims. OpenEval provides more critical assessment of the novel phosphorylation finding's functional implications.
